The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

In the narrative, the motif of light serves as a powerful symbol of continuity and human connection. The lanterns are not merely sources of illumination but represent the persistent thread of memory and community that binds the past to the present. Just as the light connects the nights, it also connects the individual stories of the townspeople, suggesting that their shared experiences and whispered confessions are integral parts of a larger, enduring tapestry. This recurring beacon underscores the theme that even in the darkness of uncertainty or isolation, the collective spirit provides warmth and guidance, ensuring that no story is told in vain and no moment is truly lost.
